Team — escalating for executive approval. Short ask below (we should include exact language for legal/finance if approved):

Customer: Nebula Health (healthcare analytics) — procurement + engineering. Deal size: ~USD 1.2M committed monthly capacity over a 12-month reservation.

Requested exceptions:
- SKU binding: Customer requests H100-class guarantee for the reserved pool. If exact SKU binding is not possible, they ask for a validated performance SLA (latency/throughput) backed by fallback credits.
- Onboarding burst: Provide a 60–90 day onboarding window where burst capacity up to 2x baseline is permitted with either (A) zero overage charges for the window, or (B) a hard overage cap of $0.08 per token-equivalent.
- Reservation hold: Allow Nebula to hold the quoted reservation and pricing for 90 days while internal approvals complete.

Proposed commercial mitigations if we approve:
- SKU: Offer H100-validated pool + an SLA clause that if we cannot provision H100 within X days, the customer receives a one-time credit equal to 5% of the first invoice.
- Burst: Approve a one-time onboarding credit covering estimated burst (up to $40k) or implement a tiered overage cap: $0.00 for first 30 days, $0.04 for days 31–60, $0.08 thereafter up to day 90.
- Hold: Allow a 90-day reservation hold conditioned on an escalation deposit (refundable credit) equal to 10% of first month commit if they don't execute by day 90.

Why approve: strategic healthcare customer, referenceability in HIPAA-adjacent workflows, likely to expand Dedicated footprint across multiple clusters. Revenue and GTM value justify a one-off exception if mitigations cover risk.

Requesting: Executive sign-off (VP or above) on the above exception path and permission to negotiate the exact credit numbers with procurement. If approved, I will instruct legal to prepare the specific term language and coordinate a DocuSign route.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Sales Manager, Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference
